mobile-native/shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/three/two/bit/ppt/reality/auth/SsoService.kt:49, :77, :104, :129 — createMobileToken / validateAndLogin / getSession / refreshSession each parse the HTTP error branch with a non-defensive `val error: SsoError = response.body()`. If the error response body is not a valid SsoError JSON object (a proxy/load-balancer HTML 502/504, an empty body, a plain-text rate-limit message, or any non-matching error shape), `response.body<SsoError>()` throws a kotlinx JsonConvert/deserialization exception.

The throw is caught by each method's outer `catch (e: Exception)`, so it is not a crash — but the surfaced result is wrong. In validateAndLogin (SsoService.kt:83-86 catch) the deep-link SSO login path sets `_authState.value = AuthState.Error(e.message ?: "Unknown error")`, so the user sees a raw serialization-exception string instead of a meaningful auth failure; getSession/refreshSession return `Result.failure(e)` where `e` is the parse error, masking the real HTTP cause (e.g. a 503).

This is an internal inconsistency, not a theoretical nit: the same class already uses the defensive pattern `runCatching { response.body<SsoError>() }.map { it.errorDescription ?: it.error }.getOrElse { "... (HTTP ${response.status.value})" }` in loginWithPassword (SsoService.kt:174), register (:202) and updateProfile (:297). The four older SSO methods were simply never updated to match. Fix vector: wrap the error-body decode in the same runCatching fallback so a non-JSON error body yields a stable 'HTTP <code>' message rather than a leaked parser exception. Confidence medium: reachability traced; depends on the server/proxy emitting a non-SsoError error body.

An empty string (`""`), a non-numeric string, a value with a thousands separator, or a `+`-prefixed literal makes `toLong()/toDouble()` throw NumberFormatException during deserialization.

These serializers were introduced specifically (per the file's own docstring, issue #2331) because a single bad monetary field decode `silently killed the whole price-tracking payload decode`. They fixed the fractional-string case but still throw on empty/malformed input, so the same blast radius remains: one unexpected monetary field value fails `response.body()` for the entire GET /api/v1/favorites or GET /api/v1/favorites/alerts response — the repo catch (FavoritesRepository) turns it into Result.failure and PriceTrackingViewModel.load (favorites/PriceTrackingViewModel.kt) renders the full-screen errorMessage state, blanking all favorites, not just the one field.

Fix vector: make the serializers truly wire-tolerant as their docstring claims — e.g. `raw.substringBefore('.').toLongOrNull() ?: 0L` (and `toDoubleOrNull() ?: 0.0`), or throw a typed field-scoped error, so a single malformed value degrades to a 0/zeroed field instead of failing the entire list decode. Confidence medium: static trace of serializer->repo->VM is certain; triggering requires the server to emit an out-of-contract decimal string (the annotated fields are non-nullable).
